issues.problem: vidā cannot be a lengthened form of viddhi (2 sg. impv. of √vid 'know', class 2). The form is the class-6 imperative vida (√vid 'find', vindati) with Vedic lengthening of the final vowel; 'gātuṃ vid' is the fixed Vedic phrase 'find the way'. The root is right but the derivation and the primary gloss 'know' are wrong.
issues.fix: gloss: find; gram: 2 sg. impv. √vid 'find' (class 6, vindati; vida with Vedic lengthening of the final vowel)

patch.value: 2 sg. impv. √vid 'find' (class 6, vindati; vida with Vedic lengthening of the final vowel)

summary: 10 units of the Mahānāmnī (SV 3.1.641-650). Tokens all match the printed text; no invented Sanskrit; the one text_flag (645, lost a of aṃśuḥ) is sound. Errors (3, all in 641): vidā derived from viddhi (√vid 'know') instead of the class-6 imperative vida of √vid 'find' (gātuṃ vid = 'find the way'), and both translations following it ('know') plus both senses of pūrvīṇām put into the text at once. Minor (18): doubled similes where the text has one na (642, 645), supplied words stated as text ('as such' 645, 'our' 644, 'you' 649), 643 Hindi gives evā hi its own verb, 644 su-vīryam mislabelled bahuvrīhi, 648 saṃnyase gram states an impossible finite form (saṃnyase vs saṃnyasyase; infinitive in -se more likely), 642 note imports the Aitareya-Āraṇyaka reading against LAYER_NOTES, 650 the pluta token is likely the second evā of the refrain. Manual decision: 648 whether to render saṃnyase as infinitive ('to take up that new praise') or keep the finite 'you take up' (no patch given for the translation). No regrouping suggested; 646 and 647 ok. Not flagged (uncertain, no variant invented): the typed र्न्न in 642 and 645 where retroflex ण्ण (ṇatva after r) would be expected in many prints; left as printed.
